We sincerely thank all reviewers for their time and effort. Their constructive comments and thoughtful feedback improved our manuscript. Moreover, we deeply appreciate their recognition of our work, which has greatly encouraged us.

Our dataset offers three main advantages:  

* **Large-scale and diverse.** The Señorita-2M dataset contains around 2 million video triplets, organized into global and local editing categories, further divided into 18 sub-categories.  

* **Strong generalization.** Editing models trained on our dataset, across four base models (CogVideoX-5B, CogVideoX-5B-I2V, Wan2.1-1.3B, and Wan2.1-14B-T2V), demonstrated robust generalization. They can even perform difficult tasks, such as shape and size editing, which were unseen in training.  

* **Community impact.** The dataset released on huggingface has received 15K total downloads, including 4.5K in last month (as of June 30, 2025). Many users have reached out with feedback, and some have successfully applied it to unified video generation and editing, showing promising results. 

We hope Señorita-2M can serve as a valuable dataset for advancing research in video editing. Once again, we sincerely thank the reviewers for their insightful feedback and kind recognition, which not only improved this work but also motivate us to continue contributing to AIGC research.

Thank you for your comments and recognition. Your feedback, such as *"the Señorita-2M dataset is a good contribution to the field"* and *"it is evident that many editing outputs display a high standard of quality, particularly in maintaining the intended modifications while preserving the integrity of the surrounding frames"*, is really encouraging. We sincerely appreciate your time and thoughtful feedback.

**Señorita-2M** is a large-scale dataset consisting of around 2 million video triplets across 18 sub-categories, covering most common tasks in the video editing. The dataset is highly diverse, featuring videos ranging from 33 to 64 frames in length, with resolutions between 336×592 and 1120×1984. It demonstrates strong generalization across various base models, including *CogVideo-5B*, *CogVideo-5B-I2V*, *Wan2.1-1.3B*, and *Wan2.1-14B-T2V*, all of which exhibit impressive editing capabilities and produce visually pleasing results. Notably, the dataset has been well received by the community, with over *15K downloads on huggingface, including 4.5K downloads in the last month*. Several recent papers have already employed Señorita-2M for training editors or developing unified generation and editing models, further highlighting its effectiveness and research value.



*Overall, Señorita-2M represents a large-scale and highly diverse dataset with strong generalization across various base models. Its increasing adoption and use in recent research highlight its value to the community. We hope this work will continue to support advancements in video editing, particularly in addressing the challenges of building high-quality, general-purpose editing datasets. Once again, we sincerely appreciate your thoughtful comments and feedback. Your insights are truly valuable and will help us further enhance the quality of our manuscript.*


 

---


***According to the NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks track guidelines, we are not allowed to include external links or updated pdfs during the rebuttal or discussion stages. As a result, we are unable to provide additional visualization results at this time. We sincerely appreciate your understanding.***


---

 

**Q1: The assertion of high quality in the dataset is somewhat overstated as a significant portion of videos, particularly in the object removal task, exhibit noticeable issues like strange blurry artifacts.**


R1: Thank you for pointing out this issue. We want to clarify the following points.

*  We acknowledge that our dataset contains some imperfections. Nevertheless, editing models trained on the dataset still demonstrated robust and reliable performance, indicating that these minor flaws did not significantly impact overall effectiveness.

* The videos you referred to appear to be part of the *object addition* task. These videos are located in the *obj_removal_videos_upload* folder because the *source videos* were generated by an object removal model and are repurposed for the object addition task. In this setup, the **source video** is a version where an object has been removed, and the **target video** is the original unedited version. Importantly, in the object addition task, the model is trained to reconstruct the original video (**target**) from the edited version (**source**), and the **source video is not used as ground truth supervision**. Therefore, any imperfections or artifacts present in the source video do not directly impact the model’s learning or the quality of the final editing results.
    
*   We plan to update the dataset by adding an aesthetic score [1,2] for each video. This will enable users to set a threshold to filter out low-quality videos during sampling, improving the overall data quality for specific applications.

 

**Q2: The fidelity of the original content preservation is questionable, as numerous videos demonstrate unintended changes in areas that were not meant to be edited . These issues lead to a lack of consistency and reliability, which can hamper the practical usability of the dataset in developing robust video editing models.**


R2: Thank you for your comments. We would like to provide the following clarifications:

*   We acknowledge that some imperfections in our dataset. These imperfections are mainly inherited from the base model. In our paper, we focused on exploring the entire pipeline for constructing a video editing dataset, including how to build specialized editing experts and how to filter out failure cases.
    
*   Manually annotating a large-scale video editing dataset is extremely challenging. Using tools like Adobe After Effects (AE) or Photoshop (PS) to edit each frame is not practical or scalable. As a result, the only feasible approach to obtain video editing triplets is by leveraging editing models to generate them. Given that our dataset includes 2 million video triplets, it is not realistic to manually filter every sample. Therefore, some imperfect videos are difficult to avoid.
    
*   We are planing to use an aesthetic scoring model [1,2] to help identify and filter out failure cases. An updated version of the dataset reflecting this improvement will be released soon.

[1] *LAION Aesthetic Predictor*. In github.

Christoph Schuhmann.

[2] *LAION-5B: An open large-scale dataset for training next generation image-text models*. In Proceedings of the Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 2022 Datasets and Benchmarks Track.

Christoph Schuhmann, Romain Beaumont, Richard Vencu, Cade Gordon, Ross Wightman, Mehdi Cherti, Theo Coombes, Aarush Katta, Clayton Mullis, Mitchell Wortsman, Patrick Schramowski, Srivatsa Kundurthy, Katherine Crowson, Ludwig Schmidt, Robert Kaczmarczyk, Jenia Jitsev.  

 


 

---

**We sincerely hope our response can address your concerns. Your comments are really constructive and help us improve the quality of our manuscript.**

Thank you for your valuable feedback and recognition. Our **Señorita-2M** dataset is a large-scale, instruction-based video editing dataset containing approximately 2 million video triplets. 

This project took several months of dedicated effort, and we were committed to ensuring its quality and usefulness. To maintain high quality and strong text-video alignment, we collaborated with four professional video editors and leveraged high-perform open-source models. Complex user prompts were simplified into clear instructions using a large language model, and a robust filtering pipeline was applied to remove low-quality samples.

Our dataset offers several key advantages:

-   **First, it is both large and diverse**, covering two main categories and 18 sub-categories of common video editing tasks. It includes videos ranging from 33 to 64 frames, with resolutions between 336×592 and 1120×1984.
    
-   **Second, it generalizes well across various base models**. We trained *CogVideo-5B*, *CogVideo-5B-I2V*, *Wan2.1-1.3B*, and *Wan2.1-14B-T2V*, all of which achieved strong editing performance using our dataset.
    
-   **Third, it has been wellreceived by the community**, with over **15K downloads** on Hugging Face, including **4.5K in the last month**. Several recent papers have used Señorita-2M  training editors or developing unified generation and editing models, demonstrating its effectiveness and research value.

 

---


***According to the NeurIPS 2025 DB track policy, we are not permitted to include external links or updated PDFs during either the rebuttal or discussion stages. As a result, we are unable to provide additional visualization results. We sincerely appreciate your understanding.***

---

 

**Q1： Imbalanced subcategories in the dataset. As illustrated in Table 2, "Object Addition" and "Object Removal" occupy 26.6% and 20.7% respectively, while some categories like "Outpainting" only constitute a small proportion at 2.0%. Such data distribution imbalance might introduce bias and create obstacles during the model training stage.**


R1: Thank you for pointing out this issue. We'd like to clarify the following:

*   **Some editing tasks (e.g., outpainting, deblur) are relatively easy to learn.** Tasks such as video outpainting and deblur are significantly easier than more complex tasks like object addition or removal. This is because the edited regions in these tasks are explicitly defined (e.g., a black masked area or the entire video), making them easier for the model to learn even from a smaller proportion of training examples.
    
*   **Tasks with higher proportions (e.g., object removal, object addition) are more common in practice.** Since users are more likely to perform tasks such as object removal or stylization, we have placed greater emphasis on these during training.
    
*   **The model performs well on the easier tasks without noticeable degradation.** Based on our evaluations, the model handles these simpler tasks effectively despite their lower percentage in the training set. *However, due to NeurIPS DB track policies, we are unable to provide visualizations.* Notably, previous image editing works such as Omni-Edit [1] and UltraEdit [2] also adopt imbalanced task distributions and report no significant performance drops across tasks. Thus, the use of an imbalanced task distribution does not appear to negatively affect overall model performance.

[1]. OmniEdit: Building Image Editing Generalist Models Through Specialist Supervision. In ICLR 2025.

Cong Wei, Zheyang Xiong, Weiming Ren, Xinrun Du, Ge Zhang, Wenhu Chen

[2]. UltraEdit: Instruction-based Fine-Grained Image Editing at Scale. In NeurIPS 2024.

Haozhe Zhao, Xiaojian Ma, Liang Chen, Shuzheng Si, Rujie Wu, Kaikai An, Peiyu Yu, Minjia Zhang, Qing Li, Baobao Chang

 

**Q2： Limited base model selection. While CogVideoX-5B-I2V is a strong image-to-video model, it generally generates low-fps videos with suboptimal temporal coherence and limited motion dynamics, which might hinder the versatility of the proposed dataset. Expanding the dataset using newer and stronger video generators could significantly improve the dataset's practicality.**

R2: Thank you for your suggestions. We would like to clarify two points:
    
*  Our dataset construction pipeline can be applied with future base models. Besides of the dataset, our another contribution is the construction pipeline of the editing experts. Our pipeline is compatible with current base models, such as HunyuanVideo, CogVideoX and Wan2.1. Our pipeline is thoroughly designed and analyzed, enabling other researchers to follow our methodology and construct even stronger datasets with newer base models and larger video collections.


* Our dataset is diverse and contains dynamic video content, with certain videos employing frame sampling at 2× or 4× rates to avoid the slow motion. Edited videos produced by our experts effectively retain these dynamic characteristics, enhancing temporal coherence and visual realism. This strategy also addresses the inherent low-fps limitations of some base models, ensuring the dataset robustly supports a broad spectrum of motion patterns.


 

---

***Thank you for your valuable comments to our paper. Your constructive suggestions are greatly appreciated.***

Additionally, we designed a filtering pipeline to remove low-quality samples and maintain the overall quality of the dataset.

Generally speaking, our dataset has the following strengths. First, it is a large-scale and diverse dataset. It contains around 2 million video triplets from 2 main categories, with 18 sub-categories. It contains the most popular video editing tasks in our dataset. The resolution and frame length of the videos is diverse. Our dataset has videos from 33 to 64 frames, with the resolution of 336×592 to 1120×1984. Second, it has good generalization on different base models. We have trained CogVideo-5B, CogVideo-5B-I2V, Wan2.1-1.3B and Wan2.1-14B-T2V, respectively, and found our datasets can make good editors based on these pretrained models. Third, it has been popular in the community. We have recieved a lot of feedback from the community users. Currently, the dataset has been downloaded from the huggingface with *15K* times, with *4.5K* downloads in last month. Some papers used our dataset to build unified generation and editing model, they demonstrate that our dataset has a good effect for their model's construction.

**Q1: In general, video restoration is defined to enhance the low-quality video instead of filling in the black pixels. In the context of this work (Line 150), restoration refers to the process of inpainting. I suggest that authors correct "Restoration" with "Inpainting" to avoid ambiguity.**

R1: Thanks for your advice. We will replace the restoration as the Inpainting in the revised paper. Your constructive suggestion help us produce better manuscripts.

 

**Q2: The common failure modes and specific tasks or scenarios where performance drops noticeably.**

**Q2.1: What are the common failure modes observed during inference with your trained models?**

R2.1: The model trained on our dataset performs well on multiple tasks. However, we still notice it has limitations. *It has higher probability to fail on processing the complex actions. For example, a man is dancing on the ground, with complex action and fast movement. When attempting to replace the man with a tiger, the model frequently fails to generate a tiger that replicates the man's dance movements.*

**Q2.2: Are there specific tasks or scenarios where performance drops noticeably?**

R2.2: We find our model is struggling with *Counter-intuitive editing instructions*. For example, the instruction "Replace a person with a horse", often lead to failures. Since human walk with two legs while horses walk with four, the model becomes confused about how to position the horse's remaining two legs. We observe that these challenging edits are strongly correlated with the generative capabilities of the base model. Specifically, we find that even asking the base model to generate a horse walking on two legs is already very difficult. Therefore, we believe that  the ability of editor will increase with the developement of the generative models.

 

**Q3: The diversity and semantically rich with the LLM-generated instructions. The linguistic or human annotation analysis of naturalness and correctness.**

**Q3.1: How diverse and semantically rich are the LLM-generated instructions?**

R3.1: Instead of only using the instruction that directly generated by LLM, we also ask LLM to generate the enhanced version. *For example, the remove tasks, we can find there are a lot of instructions in our dataset. *For example, "Delete {object}.", "Remove {object}.", "Discard {object}.", "Erase {object}.", "Clear {object}.", "Make {object} invisible.", "Remove {object} from the video."， "Make {object} disappear.", "Wipe out {object} from the video."* Therefore, by using this strategy, we make sure the diverse and semantically rich of the instructions that we provided in the dataset, preventing the overfitting risk of the editing model.


**Q3.2: Have you performed any linguistic or human annotation analysis to validate their naturalness and correctness?**

R3.2: Thanks for pointing out this question. Here, we want to clarify that: 

* When building the dataset, we have checked the llm-generated instructions with 1000 random sampled examples. Fortunately, all examples have precise instructions. 

* Generating precise instructions by LLM is reasonable, since the prompt reformulation is a relatively easy task for LLM to perform.  According to current LLM benchmark, we can find that most LLM have strong ability in language translation, paper rewriting and linguistic restatement [1, 2].

summary.value: This paper presents Señorita-2M, a large-scale, diverse, and high-quality instructional video editing dataset designed to address the limitations of existing datasets in terms of editing accuracy, temporal consistency, and sample diversity. The dataset systematically categorizes editing tasks into 2 major categories and 18 subcategories, leverages multiple task-specific experts for data generation, and implements content-level and instruction-level filtering pipelines to ensure data reliability. Models trained on the Señorita-2M dataset demonstrate superior visual quality, robust inter-frame consistency, and accurate instruction-following capabilities, validating the effectiveness of the proposed dataset.

strengths_contributions.value: This paper proposes a large scale instruction-following video editing dataset, systematically organized into 18 diverse subcategories, covering both local and global edits, which is valuable and important to the development of this field.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
1. Imbalanced subcategories in the dataset. As illustrated in Table 2, "Object Addition" and "Object Removal" occupy 26.6% and 20.7% respectively, while some categories like "Outpainting" only constitute a small proportion at 2.0%. Such data distribution imbalance might introduce bias and create obstacles during the model training stage.
2. Limited base model selection. While CogVideoX-5B-I2V is a strong image-to-video model, it generally generates low-fps videos with suboptimal temporal coherence and limited motion dynamics, which might hinder the versatility of the proposed dataset. Expanding the dataset using newer and stronger video generators [1,2] could significantly improve the dataset's practicality.

[1] Wan T, Wang A, Ai B, et al. Wan: Open and advanced large-scale video generative models[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.20314, 2025.
[2] Kong W, Tian Q, Zhang Z, et al. Hunyuanvideo: A systematic framework for large video generative models[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2412.03603, 2024.

ethical_considerations.value: No, there are no or only very minor ethics concerns

final_justification.value: My concerns have been well addressed, so I prefer to maintain my positive score of accepting this paper. A dataset of such scale is essential to the development of generative video editing.

summary.value: This submission introduces the Señorita-2M dataset, a large-scale and diverse video editing dataset designed to enhance consistency and quality in video editing tasks. The primary contribution is the development of this dataset with systematic categorization and quality-filtering processes, leading to improved model performance on video editing tasks.

strengths_contributions.value:
- The Señorita-2M dataset is a good contribution to the field as it offers a large-scale and publicly accessible resource for video editing, with two million samples that are diverse in content, resolution, and frame count, addressing the scarcity of datasets in this area.
- Upon examining the dataset, it is evident that many editing outputs display a high standard of quality, particularly in maintaining the intended modifications while preserving the integrity of the surrounding frames.
- The dataset's categorization into 2 main classes and 18 subcategories provides a comprehensive structure for various video editing tasks, ensuring a wide range of scenarios for training and testing models, which is beneficial for developing more generalized video editing capabilities.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
- The assertion of high quality in the dataset is somewhat overstated as a significant portion of videos, particularly in the object removal task, exhibit noticeable issues like strange blurry artifacts. For example, `2dbc05d7728a2e4894644a418f85386a, 7b74445894394332393b0ea4efdc0943, 8e5a5d70d675c71db1a0c317d50aefe5, 4513d753445a86c8e4d84aee6ae6ddc3, 139464ba886677abf61f0674f7f02abc`, undermining the overall quality claim. Additionally, there are instances where the edited output is entirely unsatisfactory and lacks clear interpretation, such as video `9a286a07fd0cdfee8093b969e480e6ed`.
- The fidelity of the original content preservation is questionable, as numerous videos (such as `f02506fd9fa222924d9f8176d871d085`) demonstrate unintended changes in areas that were not meant to be edited . These issues lead to a lack of consistency and reliability, which can hamper the practical usability of the dataset in developing robust video editing models.

Thanks to the authors for the reply.

I respectfully disagree with the claim 
> Nevertheless, editing models trained on the dataset still demonstrated robust and reliable performance, indicating that these minor flaws did not significantly impact overall effectiveness.

During the pre-training phase, foundational model requires clean and high-quality data, which has been validated across many settings, including LLM, VLM, image gen and so on. This has been reported by lots of tech reports, like the recent K2, GLM4.5...

That being said, I agree with other reviewers that this paper made a clear positive contribution to the field.

title.value: Señorita-2M: A High-Quality Instruction-based Dataset for General Video Editing by Video Specialists

abstract.value: Video content editing has a wide range of applications. With the advancement of diffusion-based generative models, video editing techniques have made remarkable progress, yet they still remain far from practical usability. Existing inversion-based video editing methods are time-consuming and struggle to maintain consistency in unedited regions. Although instruction-based methods have high theoretical potential, they face significant challenges in constructing high-quality training datasets - current datasets suffer from issues such as editing correctness, frame consistency, and sample diversity. To bridge these gaps, we introduce the **Señorita-2M** dataset, a large-scale, diverse, and high-quality video editing dataset. We systematically categorize editing tasks into 2 classes consisting of 18 subcategories. To build this dataset, we design four new task specialists and employ or modify 14 existing task experts to generate data samples for each subclass. In addition, we design a filtering pipeline at both the visual content and instruction levels to further enhance data quality. This approach ensures the reliability of constructed data. Finally, the **Señorita-2M** dataset comprises 2 million high-fidelity samples with diverse resolutions and frame counts. We trained multiple models using different base video models, i.e., Wan2.1 and CogVideoX-5B, on Señorita-2M, and the results demonstrate that the models exhibit superior visual quality, robust frame-to-frame consistency, and strong instruction following capability. More videos are available at: **https://senorita-2m-dataset.github.io**.
